passages.text:
1. The top ask is for Youtube to add Belarusian as a supported language. Presumably there is a
fixed cost here for Youtube as well as some ongoing ones -- the costs needed to add and
maintain a language on the platform (subtitles? interface elements? content recs? customer
support? regional compliance)? And presumably Youtube commercial=ly trades this off potential
revenue based on potential demand, and evidently that cost-benefit analysis has not historically
been in favor of Belarusian. Do we have any sense of how much the costs would be to add it
(whether fixed or ongoing), such that they could even consider it out of corporate social
responsibility?
We do not have a sense of how much the cost would be. However, it is tied to how big the
market is in a particular country. That determines how much YouTube wants to invest in a
particular country. So correct, this is why monetization in Belarus and Moldova has been a lower
priority for YT. The areas as you outline above are tied to labor/ level of effort of YT staff and
product features. Once YT decides it wants to add a language, product folks will do that and
they will take care of subtitles, interfact, etc. For other issues like policy compliance and
customer support, I think it would be a lower level of effort and won't be tied to 1 country.
Typically, there is 1 regional program covering a sub-region for Eastern Europe from a policy
perspective. It is unclear how many staff will need to support Belarusian language from the
customer support side to ensure that when issues arise, YT can support its users and ensure it
is compliant with content IYT's terms of service, but again, customer support personnel do not
support one country, typically. I do think this could be part of TY's broader social impact /
google.org efforts to increase access to information and opportunities to rising democracies.
2. When we say that adding Belarusian could support independent media, would this be for (1)
for media actors to pay youtube to play ads promoting their content, or (2) media actors to
upload content and then receive ad revenues based on its popularity, or both? If it is both, am I
understanding correctly that in order to do
(1) you NEED for the language of the ad to be a youtube supported language, whereas they are
free to upload content in Belarussian currently, and even get ad revenue for it, just not for views
from inside Russia?
It is for both. It is for content creators to be able to place ads, promote their content, receive
revenue for it, and reach their targeted audience. In Belarus, right now the content is mostly in
Russian, not Belarussian, and is perceived to be controlled by the Lukashenka regime. Content
creators can currently upload / publish content in Belarusian, but they also need to be able to
promote (e.g., place small dollar ads, run ad campaigns) and make $ off of content in
Belarusian to reach a targeted audience inside Belarus and sustain their operations. The lack of
support for Belarusian language coupled with the regime's blocking of websites makes it very
difficult for users to discover content in Belarusian language from independent media and civil
society organizations through search results or content recommendations.
In Russia, it is a different story. As I understand, YouTube is available and the mobile market is
dominated by Android. Google does not have a physical presence or the ability to process
payments for people located in the country to our sanctions policy on Russia. We have been
working with exiles of this country living in Eastern Europe to be able to communicate and

broadcast credible information inside Russia. YT may be able to help in this regard, however,
don't know how much given the current inability to process payments inside of Russia
3. Question in terms of monetizing content from viewers inside Russia. as a policy position, do
we hold the view that the marginal benefits of having Belarussian content creators get ad
revenue from viewers within Russia wouldbe greater than the marginal costs that occur when
malign actors outside of Russia profit by spreading disinformation to viewers inside Russia?
Also, is Youtube even able to separate the deactivation of "in russia" views for channels located
outside the country vs. those located inside the country, or does it simply have to deactivate
monetization at large for views inside Russia, regardless of where the channel is located? what
I'm trying to get at is that any policy that allows content monetization for independent media
outlets fleeing authoritarian regimes is also going to allow content monetization for other groups
as well, and making sure we're making a recommendation based on how things net out overall.
We cannot make a policy recommendation on this. This is up for YouTube to decide. However, I
would agree with this assessment. We simply are hoping that content creators have equal
access to opportunity to reach their audience and monetize their content.
4. There is also an ask for youtube to allow monetization in Moldova. Could you please clarify
what this means? Presumably it's not a language issue as individuals can both upload content
and push out ads in Romanian? It's a geographical issue where youtube simply says that
channels in a certain geography cannot do ads? If that is true, would welcome any information
we have on the costs of adding a new geography (regulatory, etc.).
This is not a language or geography issue - it is purely an access and an opportunity issue.
Moldova is not currently a part of YouTube's Partner Program which allows local creators to
monetize their content. We hope that YT considers allowing small independent media outlets
and content creators to monetize off of their channels in order to reach a broader audience in
Moldova and sustain their operations.
